You are translating an SRT subtitle file to Dhivehi.

The input mixes Japanese (Japanese (kanji + hiragana/katakana) script) and English code-switched speech.

About Dhivehi, the language to write in:
- This audio is in DHIVEHI (also called Maldivian, ISO code: dv), the language of the Maldives. It is NOT Sinhala (Sri Lankan).
- Dhivehi uses the Thaana script (e.g. ދިވެހި, އަޅުގަނޑު, ވަރަށް, ހުރިހާ). Thaana letters look like ހ ށ ނ ރ ބ ޅ ކ އ ވ މ ފ ދ ތ ލ ގ ޏ ސ ޑ ޒ ޓ ޔ ޕ ޖ ޗ ޘ ޙ ޚ ޛ ޜ ޝ ޞ ޟ ޠ ޡ ޢ ޣ ޤ ޥ.
- Do NOT output Sinhala script (e.g. ක ග ට ද න ම ය ර ල ව ස හ ඈ ඉ උ එ ඔ — these are WRONG). If you produce Sinhala characters anywhere, you have made an error.

CRITICAL: Preserve the SRT structure EXACTLY:
- Same number of cues, in the same order.
- Same cue numbers.
- Same timestamps (do not modify the HH:MM:SS,mmm values).
- Same speaker labels (e.g. "Speaker 1:" prefixes).

Translate the spoken text content:
- Translate Japanese to natural conversational Dhivehi.
- Translate English words and phrases to Dhivehi too.
- Aim for natural Dhivehi, not literal word-for-word.
- Write Dhivehi in Thaana.

Output ONLY the translated SRT. No preamble, no code fences, no commentary.
